replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, write the equation in standard form: ax² + bx + c = 0. Then, use the quadratic formula x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / (2a). Calculate the discriminant (b² - 4ac) first to see if there are real solutions. If the discriminant is positive, you get two real roots; if zero, one real root; if negative, complex roots.

To find stationary points, take the first derivative f'(x) of the function. Set f'(x) = 0 and solve for x. These x-values are critical points. Then, plug them back into f(x) to get the corresponding y-values. You can also use the second derivative test to determine if they’re maxima or minima.
